concept.name: Concept drift
concept.definition: An unforeseeable change over time in the underlying relationship between inputs and outputs — formally, a change in P(y|X) — so that the mapping a model learned no longer holds even for identical inputs. The concept-drift literature (e.g., Lu et al., IEEE TKDE) organizes the field into drift detection, drift understanding, and drift adaptation.
concept.intuition: The rules of the game changed: the same setup that used to mean 'buy' now means nothing — the model's knowledge itself is outdated, not just its inputs.
concept.mechanics: Drift may be sudden (structural breaks, rule changes), gradual, incremental, or recurring (regimes). Detection uses error-rate monitoring and statistical change tests; adaptation uses incremental learning, sliding windows, or ensemble reweighting. In trading, crowding out of an anomaly, a central-bank regime shift, or a market-structure rule change are canonical causes.
concept.formula: Concept drift between times t0 and t1: P_{t1}(y|X) ≠ P_{t0}(y|X) — the conditional distribution of the label given the features changes, with or without a change in P(X).
concept.failure_modes: Concept drift can be invisible in input statistics (P(X) unchanged), so input-only monitoring misses it while errors accumulate. Adaptation mechanisms risk chasing noise: retraining on every apparent drift whipsaws the model and destroys stability.
concept.misconceptions: Concept drift is not the model 'forgetting' or a bug to be patched once — in non-stationary environments like markets it is a permanent operating condition requiring continuous detection and adaptation. Retraining on more old data does not help when the old relationship itself is obsolete.
concept.example: A carry-trade signal learned when central banks moved in sync stops working after policy divergence: identical interest-rate inputs now map to different outcomes, and only error-rate monitoring reveals the shift.

citations.source: Lu et al., 'Learning under Concept Drift: A Review' (IEEE TKDE, 2018)
